methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective biomarker study on prospectively banked plasma from 54 resected PDAC patients (Atlantic Cancer Consortium Biobank, QEII Health Sciences Centre) with laboratory personnel blinded to clinical outcomes and radiologist blinded for deltaHU. Pre-specified primary outcome (6-month mortality) and a priori selection of sAXL and tumour grade for multivariable Cox are methodologically sound. Key weaknesses: only 7 events at 6 months supporting a two-variable Cox model (events per variable well below rule-of-thumb), no external validation, single-center, heterogeneous neoadjuvant status (46%) not adjusted, cut-offs derived and evaluated in the same cohort with Youden index (risk of optimism bias despite bootstrap CIs). Statistical approach uses time-dependent ROC, Kaplan-Meier/log-rank, and Cox with bootstrap CIs but lacks proper internal validation (e.g., cross-validation) and multiplicity adjustment.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The motivation to identify preoperative predictors of futile PDAC resection is highly clinically relevant, and a simple plasma ELISA is attractive as a translational tool. However, the sample size and absence of external validation make the finding hypothesis-generating at best; the authors frame it as exploratory. Oxford LoE is 4 for a single-center retrospective biomarker cohort with no validation set.

reporting_quality.justification: This is a prognostic biomarker study and maps to REMARK; adherence is not explicitly claimed but many REMARK items (patient selection, biomarker assay details, cut-off derivation, outcome definitions, multivariable modeling, limitations) are partially addressed. Gaps: no reporting of inter-assay CV, no pre-specified cut-point rationale (derived and tested in the same cohort), no CONSORT-style flow for the 91 to 54 reduction beyond a brief note, and no discovery/validation separation. No data or code availability statement is provided.

novelty_literature.justification: Soluble AXL has been studied as a PDAC diagnostic biomarker by Martinez-Bosch et al. [10]; the current work extends this to a prognostic application for 6-month post-resection mortality and compares to CA19-9, plus an exploratory biophysical (deltaHU) subanalysis. This is a meaningful extension of prior work but not field-defining, and the deltaHU subanalysis was negative.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with explicit framing as exploratory, a logical flow from biomarker discovery to cut-off derivation to survival analyses. Figures (ROC curves, Kaplan-Meier, deltaHU examples) and tables are referenced in context. Two redacted phrases ('aggressive [REDACTED]') slightly disrupt flow but do not impair comprehension. The abstract contains a minor grammatical error ('while it 253.3 U/mL').

key_strengths: Blinded biomarker assays and blinded radiologic deltaHU assessment
A priori pre-specification of sAXL plus tumour grade for multivariable Cox modeling
Use of time-dependent ROC and bootstrap confidence intervals, acknowledging small-sample fragility
Direct comparison to the FDA-approved CA19-9 benchmark in the same cohort
Honest framing as an exploratory validation step with explicit acknowledgement of limitations
key_concerns: Only 7 six-month mortality events supporting a two-variable Cox model, well below events-per-variable guidance
Cut-offs (sAXL 40.26 ng/mL; CA19-9 253.3 U/mL) derived via Youden on the same cohort used for evaluation, with no external validation
Heterogeneous neoadjuvant exposure (46%) and margin/grade distributions not adjusted as confounders
Log-rank for sAXL did not reach significance (p=0.088) despite the positive multivariable HR, underscoring fragility
No REMARK checklist use and no data/code deposition
chief_reviewer.rationale: A carefully written exploratory biomarker study whose small event count and lack of external validation limit claims; fits a mid-tier oncology journal with major revisions to add REMARK alignment and a validation strategy.
